text:
Taylor Hall plays his 1,000th NHL game tonight, and he does it in Helsinki. The Hurricanes and Kraken meet in the NHL's Global Series in Finland, which NHL.com's Tracey Myers called the perfect stage for it. It is a fitting road for a career that has wandered: a first overall pick in 2010, a Hart Trophy in New Jersey in 2018, and stops all over the league since. Milestones are not part of our numbers. This one does not need to be.

The hockey part looks lopsided. Carolina sits atop the NHL standings and plays like it: 58% of the five-on-five expected goals, the quality of the chances, 4.11 goals a game, and a 9-2 rout of Chicago before flying over. Our honest caveat is that the results are running ahead of even that excellent process, with a +34 goal difference on +23.8 expected, and finishing and goaltending adding a few goals each. Pyotr Kochetkov has been very good (.920, 9.8 goals saved above expected), Jackson Blake has points in nine straight, Logan Stankoven has 12 in his last ten, and Alexander Nikishin had two points in his season debut. Jordan Staal (calf) is out until early December.

Seattle arrives with a 45% share of the expected goals and a roster in flux. The Kraken traded Shane Wright to Nashville for Matthew Wood earlier this month, and Jared McCann (lower body) is out until January. The best reason to watch them is Berkly Catton, the 20-year-old on an eight-game point streak with ten points in his last ten. Philipp Grubauer starts after a rough stretch: .866 and 4.8 goals worse than expected over his last five. Kaapo Kakko, a Finn, has been planning the team's off-ice time in Helsinki, per Tom Gulitti.

Both teams had four days off, so nobody can blame the travel. Our Sleeper is Mark Jankowski, filling in for Staal on the third line, whose 4.5 expected goals in his last ten games lead all depth forwards; we give him a 23% chance to score. Our numbers have Carolina at 3.58 expected goals and Seattle at 2.52.
headline: Taylor Hall's 1,000th, a long way from home
